reproduction_target: Reproduce, from the 29 cockroach/termite genomes and proteomes (three published solitary cockroach genomes plus new genomes reported in Jones et al. 2025 and Liu et al. 2025) and from the 285 newly generated brain RNA-seq libraries of 14 species, the comparative-genomics and comparative-transcriptomics results: ancestral state reconstruction of the termite worker caste (ape/corHMM/phytools), the standardised ontogeny networks and the SPL / Ontogenic Complexity Metric, the time-calibrated species phylogeny (PRANK + FASconCAT-G + IQ-TREE + MCMCTREE/PAML + Tracer), OrthoFinder orthology, the selection analyses (Gblocks-trimmed SCO alignments, CodeML dN/dS, HyPhy RELAX and aBSREL including the 100-iteration random-foreground permutation, FastTree gene trees for remaining HOGs), the MCMCglmm phylogenetic mixed models of dN/dS, k, OCM and SPL, the CAFE5 gene-family expansion/contraction analysis and its model selection, the MCMCglmm gene-family-size models identifying the 44 and then 10 convergent families, the odorant-receptor re-annotation and phylogeny (BITACORA, hmmbuild, mafft, pfam_scan, DeepTMHMM, mafft-einsi, trimal, IQTREE2, iTOL, Possvm, aBSREL), the CpGo/e methylation proxy and its PCA, the RNA-seq processing chain (Trimmomatic, HISAT2, SAMtools, htseq-count, DESeq2), the wTO/CoDiNA caste-specific and differential co-expression networks and their Cytoscape visualisation, the DESeq2 caste-biased DEG sets and cross-species orthologue overlaps, the FactoMineR PCAs, the OR-DEG connectivity proportions, the bedtools TE-content analysis, the lme4/emmeans models of gene properties, the PfamScan/TopGO GO enrichment, the SuperExactTest toolkit overlaps, the blastp reciprocal-best-hit functional annotation, and the CCHamide (HOG001851) gene tree. Insect collection and rearing, brain dissection, and RNA extraction / library preparation / NovaSeq sequencing are out of scope (W).
granularity_note: The main bioRxiv text contains no Methods section; all methods live in the Supplementary Materials PDF (media-1.pdf, 49 pages, 'Materials and Methods' pp. 2-18), which was downloaded and read in full. One step per named tool invocation or named analysis block. Tool chains that are always run together within a single named Methods paragraph and share one input/output pair (e.g. PRANK + FASconCAT-G + IQ-TREE for the species tree; mafft-einsi + trimal + IQTREE2 for the OR phylogeny; HISAT2 + SAMtools name-sorting) are collapsed into a single step. Purely arithmetic post-processing (Benjamini-Hochberg correction, dividing link counts by gene counts) is folded into its parent step. |S| = 38 computational steps, |W| = 3 wet-lab steps.

steps.label: Field collection and laboratory rearing of 4 cockroach and 10 termite species across BAM Berlin, MNHN Paris, UNESP Rio Claro, UFABC Sao Paulo, OIST Okinawa and Universite Sorbonne Paris Nord, with stated diets, temperatures, humidity, light regimes, colony pooling rules and morphological caste/sex determination
Brain dissection of 1492 individuals in ice-cold PBS under a stereoscope, snap-freezing in liquid nitrogen, pooling up to 5 brains (10 for A. pacificus workers) into 285 RNA samples

Total RNA extraction (RNeasy Plus Mini Kit with gDNA eliminator), Qubit quantification, Bioanalyzer RIN QC (median 8.5), NEBNext Poly(A) mRNA enrichment, NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA Library Prep, paired-end 2x100 bp sequencing at 50 M reads/sample on a NovaSeq 6000 S4 XP v1.5 flowcell at the DRESDEN-concept Genome Center

Ancestral state reconstruction of the termite worker caste as a binary trait (true worker vs pseudergate) on the named published tree file '73_iqtree_majority_rule_phytools_updated.tree' from Hellemans et al. (2024) supplementary, with polytomies resolved as branches 1/1000000 of maximum tree height; ML fitting with the 'ace' function of R package ape v5.6-1 under ER and ARD, plus 2- and 3-rate-category ARD via corHMM v2.8, model selection by Akaike weight with 'aic.w' from phytools v1.2-0

Reconstruction of standardised termite/cockroach ontogeny networks for 29 species from the literature (males and females separately; sister species used for 10 species and same-family relatives for 3), with hand-applied inclusion rules for mature-colony pathways, secondary reproductive classes and unclear ontogenetic connections

Computation of the shortest characteristic path length (SPL, Boccaletti et al. 2006) and the number of terminal stages on the standardised ontogeny networks, and derivation of the Ontogenic Complexity Metric (OCM) used as the sociality proxy in Fig. 1d

MCMCglmm phylogenetic mixed models of OCM and SPL against social category (Social FW vs Social TW; solitary and subsocial set to NA), simplified from model S1 with phylogenetic and non-phylogenetic random effects, 13 million generations, thinning 5000, burn-in 3 million

Species tree inference from 826 single-copy orthologs: alignment with PRANK v.170427 ('-F'), concatenation with FASconCAT-G v1.05.1, topology inference with IQ-TREE v2.1.3 using the MFP+MERGE algorithm

Bayesian divergence-time estimation with MCMCTREE (PAML 4.9g) on the concatenated protein supermatrix: 14 fossil soft-bound calibrations (Table S8) with 2.5% tail probability, root prior 323.2 Ma, Hessian first under Poisson then under WAG+Gamma (fix_alpha=0, alpha=0.5, ncatG=4), usedata=3 then usedata=2, independent lognormal clock, 100,000,000 iterations sampled every 100 with 10% burn-in, 3 replicate chains checked in Tracer v1.7.1

Retrieval of the longest isoform from the published proteomes of B. germanica, P. americana and D. punctata and from the new genomes of B. orientalis, two Cryptocercus and 23 termites (Jones et al. 2025; Liu et al. 2025); no tool, script or accession named
Gene orthology prediction across the 29 proteomes with OrthoFinder v2.5.4, producing 33338 hierarchical orthologous groups (HOGs) and the OrthoFinder species tree used downstream
Alignment of single-copy orthologs with PRANK v.170427 ('-F') and trimming with Gblocks v0.91b ('-b5=h')

dN/dS estimation on trimmed SCO alignments with CodeML (PAML 4.9j) using the fully listed config (runmode=0, seqtype=1, CodonFreq=2, ndata=1, clock=0, model=1, NSsites=0, fix_omega=0, omega=.4, cleandata=0)

Tests of relaxed and intensified selection with HyPhy RELAX and of episodic positive selection with HyPhy aBSREL v2.5.41, under (i) each branch as foreground and (ii) the three branches leading to bifurcated-development termites as foreground, plus a null calibration repeating RELAX 100 times with three randomly assigned foreground termite branches; Benjamini-Hochberg correction
Alignment of all remaining (non-SCO) HOGs as above, per-HOG phylogeny reconstruction with FastTree v2.1.11 (default options), and dN/dS reconstruction with CodeML using the same config parameters

Phylogenetic generalized linear mixed models (R package MCMCglmm v2.34) of SCO dN/dS, remaining-HOG dN/dS and the RELAX k parameter against sociality and ecological traits, following model S1 with exponential link, phylogenetic / species / orthogroup random effects, 13 million (SCO) and 1.3 million (HOG) generations, thinning 5000, burn-in 3 million / 300000, three prior settings (parameter-expanded, flat, inverse-Wishart) and inverse-gamma residual priors (shape=scale=0.001)

Gene family expansion/contraction analysis with CAFE5 (no version pinned) on 17438 of 33338 HOGs using the fossil-calibrated tree, including the model-selection sweep over gamma categories K=1..10 and branch-specific lambda clusters L=1..6 (50 repeats per model, 150-250 repeats for the 48 branch trees), k-means clustering of branch lambdas with R packages cluster v2.1.4 and factoextra v1.0.7, and the final model with K=3, L=1, lambda = 0.24314831349735

MCMCglmm (Gaussian family) models of the 569 significantly size-evolving gene families against ontogeny and social category, with phylogenetic-only and phylogenetic+non-phylogenetic random effects, Inverse-Wishart and expanded priors, Gamma residual prior and Benjamini-Hochberg correction; plus the manual filter retaining families only where M. darwiniensis and D. longilabius cluster nearer the bifurcated median, and the parallel screen of the 15900 CAFE-ineligible HOGs filtered at >=13 copies (1865 families)

Odorant receptor re-annotation with BITACORA v1.3 (BLAST + HMMER, genome and proteome mode, default settings except the length filter omitted) against a custom OR database built from D. punctata, B. germanica, D. melanogaster, A. mellifera and A. lucorum sequences, with the HMM profile built using hmmbuild v3.3.2 and mafft --auto v7.397
Filtering of curated OR gene models for the 7tm_6 domain with pfam_scan.pl (default settings, pfam1.6, PFAM database v37.1) and for transmembrane domains with the DeepTMHMM 1.0 hosted service

OR phylogeny: alignment of all OR sequences with mafft-einsi v7.505, trimming with trimal v1.4.1 (-automated1), inclusion of one B. germanica GR sequence as outgroup, and maximum-likelihood inference with IQTREE2 v2.1.3 ('-m TEST')
Visualization and annotation of the OR gene tree with the iTOL v7.2.1 web service and the R package itol.toolkit v1.1.7
Clustering of ORs into gene clusters with Possvm v1.2 at default settings, using the OR gene tree as input
Per-OR-cluster realignment, gene-tree reconstruction (as in C18) and test for episodic positive selection with HyPhy aBSREL v2.5.41 without specifying test branches

Estimation of protein-coding gene methylation proxy CpGo/e (observed vs expected CG counts), per-species density plots with base R plot(density()), mode estimation with Modes() from LaplacesDemon v16.1.6, principal component analysis of SCO CpGo/e with prcomp() from stats v4.4.1, and plotting with base R v4.2.0 and ggplot2 v3.4.4
Adapter and quality trimming of all 285 RNA-seq libraries with TRIMMOMATIC v0.39 using ILLUMINACLIP:TruSeq3-PE-2.fa:2:30:10 and otherwise default parameters
Mapping of trimmed reads to the respective species genome with HISAT2 v2.1.1 (indices built with hisat2-build) and name-sorting of the resulting SAM files with SAMtools v1.17

Read counting per gene with htseq-count v2.0.9 against the per-species gff3 annotations, using --stranded no, feature type 'gene' and id attribute 'ID', producing per-species count tables plus condition files (species, caste/stage, sex, replicate ID)
Normalization of read counts for each of the 14 species using the DESeq2 median-of-ratios method (DESeq2 version not stated)

Construction of caste-specific signed weighted topological overlap (WTO) co-expression networks with the R package wTO v2.0.2, merging balanced male and female samples, including all transcriptome genes and no bootstrapping; 34 caste-specific termite networks and 8 stage-specific cockroach networks

Differential network analysis with the R package CoDiNA v1.1.2 at default parameters with median-quantile internal and external node-clustering cutoffs, both as a full comparison of all caste networks per species and as pairwise worker-vs-reproductive comparisons for 13 species (Z. nevadensis excluded), followed by the rule assigning a gene to a caste when the majority of its links are caste-specific and discarding genes specific to more than one caste

Visualization of reduced OR + DEG co-expression networks in Cytoscape v3.10.3 with prefuse force-directed layout weighted by absolute correlation coefficient, edges filtered at |r| > 0.4 and nodes retained at degree >= 5 (with a per-panel exception of edge weight 0.6 / degree 32 for A. pacificus workers)

Pairwise differential gene expression between castes within each species with DESeq2 (version not stated), caste-only design with sexes merged, non-expressed genes removed, BH-adjusted p < 0.05 and minimum log fold change of zero; followed by cross-species identification of shared caste-biased genes via orthologue-ID overlaps

Principal component analyses of normalized read counts per species with the R packages FactoMineR (version not stated) and factoextra v1.0.7 over the first 5 components by caste, sex and replicate, plus the species-normalized PCA in which SCO counts are averaged per caste and then averaged and scaled across castes for 13 species

Counting of co-expression links between caste-specific ORs and shared caste-biased DEGs using the Netvis function of the wTO package, excluding OR-OR and DEG-DEG links and links below a wTO threshold of 0.33, then normalizing by the number of ORs and the number of DEGs, computed separately for all ORs, cluster-1 ORs and cluster-2 ORs across 9 termite species

Counting of transposable elements in the 10 kb upstream region of each gene with bedtools v2.30.0 intersect, using the TE annotations of Liu et al. (2025) available for only one solitary (B. orientalis) and one subsocial (C. meridianus) species

Generalized linear mixed models (R package lme4, version not stated) of gene properties (dN/dS, k, upstream TE count) following model S2 (Group * ExprBias + 1|Species), with group contrasts computed via the emmeans package v1.10.0

GO-term annotation and enrichment: per-species domain annotation of longest isoforms with PfamScan (version not stated), mapping of Pfam IDs to GO terms using the Mitchell et al. (2015) documentation and custom-made scripts, generation of TopGO-compatible universe files, TopGO v2.50.0 objects for Biological Process and Molecular Function built with 'annFUN.gene2GO' and a custom 'GOmap' script, and significance testing with the 'weight01' algorithm and Fisher test at alpha = 0.05

Significance testing of overlapping orthologue sets between castes and across species with the R package SuperExactTest v1.1.0, applied to the enumerated overlap patterns (worker/reproductive 9/9, 7/9, 5/9; soldier/reproductive 8/8, 6/8, 4/8; worker/soldier 9/9, 7/9, 5/9; cockroach 2/2), restricted to HOGs with at least one orthologous gene across the compared species

Functional annotation of all annotated proteins by reciprocal best BLAST hits with blastp v.2.12.0+ against the proteomes of D. melanogaster, A. mellifera and T. castaneum (no proteome versions or accessions, no BLAST thresholds stated), followed by the manual decision cascade (reciprocal hit, then best hit, then A. mellifera / T. castaneum, else 'unclear') and hand classification of orthogroups into JH-, 20E-, insulin-related and nine further functional categories

Alignment and gene-tree reconstruction for HOG001851 (CCHamide receptor candidates) using the same methods applied to ORs, rooted with CCHamide-1 receptor sequences identified by reciprocal best BLAST hit against D. melanogaster CCHa1-R (FBpp0086052)
Assembly and formatting of the multi-panel main-text figures in Inkscape v.1.3.2 (interactive vector editing; no source SVGs, no panel provenance, no recorded operations)

headline.static_readiness: 0/39 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 1/39 (3%) readiness upper bound at stage 1: (n_R + n_RI) / |S| = (0 + 1) / 39. The single RI step is C1 (ancestral state reconstruction), the only computational step whose input is a publicly retrievable, explicitly named artifact - the tree file '73_iqtree_majority_rule_phytools_updated.tree' from the supplementary material of Hellemans et al. (2024). Every other step scores data = 0 because the paper contains NO data availability statement, NO code availability statement, and NO accession of any kind: the 285 newly generated brain RNA-seq libraries (a substantial new dataset produced at the DRESDEN-concept Genome Center) have no BioProject/SRA/ENA/GEO identifier anywhere in the main text, the 49-page supplementary PDF or the bioRxiv landing page, and the 29 genomes/proteomes are referenced only as 'Jones et al. 2025; Liu et al. 2025' with no accession repeated here. Method reporting itself is unusually detailed for this genre - 33 of 39 computational steps carry an exact prose version pin, model configs (CodeML control parameters, MCMCTREE priors and chain lengths, MCMCglmm formulae and burn-in, htseq-count flags, Trimmomatic ILLUMINACLIP string, CAFE5 lambda to 17 significant figures) are stated verbatim - so the binding constraint is deposition, not description. Unexecuted; under-claims by construction - Tier-1 cannot credit an undeclared-but-present dependency, nor a deposit that exists but is not cited.
headline.coverage: computational coverage |S| / (|S| + |W|) = 39 / 42 = 93%; 3 wet-lab steps (insect collection and rearing, brain dissection, RNA extraction and NovaSeq sequencing) are OOS. Evidence coverage: the main bioRxiv text carries no Methods at all; the full Materials and Methods was read from the supplementary PDF (media-1.pdf, 49 pages), so step extraction is complete rather than partial.

gaps.where: whole paper - main text, supplementary Materials and Methods, bioRxiv landing page; affects computational steps C2-C39
gaps.missing: There is no data availability statement of any kind. A full-text scan of the JATS XML (90513 bytes), the rendered v1 .full HTML (235652 bytes) and the 49-page supplementary PDF returns zero occurrences of 'availability', 'accession', 'deposited', 'BioProject', 'PRJNA/PRJEB/PRJDB', 'GEO', 'SRA', 'ENA', 'figshare', 'Zenodo' or 'Dryad'. The study generated 285 new brain RNA-seq libraries (1492 dissections, 14 species) and uses 29 genomes/proteomes, and none of these inputs is given an identifier in this paper. The Methods state only that 'SAM files were converted into BAM files and stored with the raw reads and the gene counts' - stored, not deposited. This sets data = 0 on 38 of 39 computational steps and is the single dominant blocker.
gaps.how_to_close: Add a data availability statement giving the BioProject/SRA (or ENA) accession for the 285 RNA-seq libraries, the assembly and annotation accessions (or an explicit pointer to the accessions in Jones et al. 2025 and Liu et al. 2025) for all 29 genomes and proteomes, and a repository DOI for the derived tables (count matrices, condition files, HOG assignments, DEG lists, wTO/CoDiNA networks, OR annotations).

gaps.missing: There is no code availability statement and no repository URL (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Zenodo, Software Heritage) anywhere in the paper, supplement or landing page. Not one of the ~40 analyses is backed by a deposited script, notebook, workflow file or command log, despite the pipeline spanning at least 35 distinct tools and several bespoke procedures.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the analysis scripts (or at minimum the command log and R scripts) in a public repository with a tagged release and cite it in a Code availability section.

gaps.missing: Several bespoke artefacts and procedures are described in prose but neither released nor fully specified: the custom-made scripts and 'GOmap' script for Pfam-to-GO mapping and TopGO universe generation (C35, named as custom in the Methods); the OR reference database assembled from five species (C16, no accession list); the standardised ontogeny networks and the SPL / OCM computation (C2, C3 - no tool named, no formula for OCM in the Methods, networks not deposited); the 100-iteration random-foreground RELAX permutation (C11); the 'closer to the median of bifurcated species' filter used to reduce 44 gene families to 10 (C15, criterion not quantified); the CpGo/e calculation (C22); the caste-assignment majority rule over CoDiNA links (C28); and the OR-DEG link-proportion computation (C32).
gaps.how_to_close: Release each custom script with its input and output files, and quantify the median-proximity filter and the caste-assignment tie-breaking rule.

gaps.where: C14 (CAFE5), C26 and C30 (DESeq2), C31 (FactoMineR), C34 (lme4), C35 (PfamScan), C11 (HyPhy RELAX), C2/C3/C7 (no tool named)
gaps.missing: Version pins are otherwise excellent but absent for a small set of load-bearing tools: CAFE5 is named by major version only, DESeq2 is used for both normalization and all differential expression with no version, lme4 and FactoMineR carry no version, PfamScan is unversioned in C35 (a Pfam 1.6 / PFAM v37.1 pin appears only in C17), and the HyPhy release providing RELAX is not stated separately from aBSREL v2.5.41. C2, C3 and C7 name no software at all.
gaps.how_to_close: State the version of every tool and R package used, and name the software (or release the script) used for isoform selection, ontogeny network construction and SPL/OCM computation.

gaps.missing: No random seed is stated for any stochastic procedure: the MCMCglmm chains (C4, C13, C15), the MCMCTREE MCMC replicates (C6), IQ-TREE / IQTREE2 model selection and tree search (C5, C18), the 100-iteration random-branch RELAX permutation (C11), and the CAFE5 repeated optimisations and k-means clustering (C14). Convergence checks are described (Tracer ESS, lambda convergence over 50-250 repeats), so agreement is expected to be distributional rather than exact.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the seeds, or state explicitly that agreement is to be judged distributionally and provide the posterior/summary outputs for comparison.

gaps.missing: External reference resources are pinned inconsistently. Pinned: PFAM database v37.1 with pfam1.6 (C17), DeepTMHMM 1.0 (C17). Unpinned: the per-species reference genomes and hisat2 indices (C24) and gff3 annotations (C25), the TE annotations taken from Liu et al. 2025 (C33), the Pfam release used by PfamScan in C35, the Mitchell et al. 2015 Pfam-to-GO mapping snapshot (C35), and the D. melanogaster / A. mellifera / T. castaneum proteomes used for reciprocal best BLAST (C37). Fossil ages were retrieved from the Paleobiology Database with an access date (October 2023) but no query or download snapshot (C6).
gaps.how_to_close: State a versioned accession or release identifier (and ideally a checksum) for every reference genome, annotation, proteome and database, and deposit the Paleobiology Database query result used for the 14 calibrations.

gaps.where: C7, C8, C33 and all genome-derived steps
gaps.missing: The genome assemblies, gene annotations and TE annotations for the new B. orientalis, two Cryptocercus and 23 termite genomes are externalised to Jones et al. (2025) and Liu et al. (2025) by citation only, with no accession, version or assembly identifier repeated here. Reproduction therefore depends on resolving two separate papers and hoping their deposits match the versions used.
gaps.how_to_close: Repeat the assembly and annotation accessions (with versions) in this paper's data availability statement and state which assembly release was used.

gaps.missing: Four steps depend on interactive or hosted software with no recorded operations: the DeepTMHMM 1.0 web service (C17), the iTOL v7.2.1 web service with itol.toolkit annotation files that are not deposited (C19), Cytoscape v3.10.3 interactive network layout (C29), and Inkscape v1.3.2 figure assembly (C39, scored X). None is proprietary in the licence sense, but each is unrecordable from prose alone.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the iTOL annotation files, the Cytoscape session (.cys) files and the source SVGs, and note the DeepTMHMM run date or use the containerised release.

gaps.missing: The sample-to-library correspondence exists only as prose. The Methods describe per-species 'condition files indicating the species name, the caste or stage name, the sex and the replicate ID for each sample' and rules about pooling colonies and merging sexes, but neither the condition files nor a sample manifest for the 285 libraries is provided, and colony/pooling composition per replicate is described only narratively (e.g. 'five family groups were pooled in one replicate', 'only one colony per sample' for seven taxa).
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the 285-row sample sheet linking each library accession to species, caste/stage, sex, replicate, colony origin and pooling composition.

gaps.missing: Insect collection and rearing across six institutions, 1492 brain dissections, and RNA extraction / library preparation / NovaSeq 6000 sequencing are wet-lab steps and are excluded from |S| as OOS. They are described in unusually good detail (diets, temperatures, humidity, instar sampling, dissection temperature and time limits, kit names, RIN values, flowcell type, target depth), so this is a scope exclusion, not a reporting gap.
gaps.how_to_close: n/a - documentation-only; no action required for computational reproducibility.
